definition: Accessibility/familiarity of a claim for an agent after exposure.
what_it_is_not: Truth, source reliability, or factual evidence.

definition: Current accessibility of corrective information for a claim.
what_it_is_not: Guaranteed belief correction.

definition: Agent's task-relevant estimate of a source's reliability.
what_it_is_not: Actual source reliability.

definition: Latent propensity to judge a claim as true at a given time.
what_it_is_not: Knowledge, ideology, or identity commitment.

definition: Contextual decision weight placed on accuracy when acting/sharing.
what_it_is_not: General rationality or System 2 activation.

definition: Count or history of exposures of an agent to an information item.
what_it_is_not: Familiarity itself.

definition: Observed or simulated action indicating whether an item is shared.
what_it_is_not: Belief or endorsement.

definition: Signed valence assigned to an event-relevant information unit for the M1 reference selection task.
what_it_is_not: Truth value, factuality, political ideology, or emotional state of a person.

definition: Reference policy controlling which valence-compatible information units are preferentially selected from a fixed event pool.
what_it_is_not: A measured newsroom bias score, misinformation rate, ownership effect, or platform ranking parameter.

definition: Mean signed valence of the information units actually exposed after editorial selection.
what_it_is_not: Ground truth, total event valence, or a person's opinion.

definition: Bounded M1 reference state representing the current evaluation of an event or issue after the observed information sample.
what_it_is_not: Claim truth belief B, knowledge, ideology, affect diagnosis, or a calibrated population attitude.

definition: Reference encoding of a semantically equivalent confirmation versus refutation presentation.
what_it_is_not: Truth value, factuality, editorial selection, or emotional valence.

definition: Task-specific relation between an agent's prior stance and the semantic stance of the current message.
what_it_is_not: Stable ideology, party identity, personality, or a global confirmation-bias score.

definition: Latent M1.E2 probability of an active engagement response under the reference presentation task.
what_it_is_not: M0 Share probability, platform CTR, endorsement, or a calibrated population engagement rate.

definition: Reference observable corresponding to an active stated response such as like, share, or comment versus ignore.
what_it_is_not: M0 Share, observed platform behavior, or endorsement.

definition: Binary precomputed reference cue distinguishing lower-negativity/control from higher-negativity headline conditions in M1.E3.
what_it_is_not: A runtime sentiment score, LIWC proportion, truth value, misinformation label, experienced emotion, political orientation, or calibrated effect size.

definition: Latent M1.E3 probability of opening/clicking the full item conditional on one registered PreviewImpression.
what_it_is_not: Observed population CTR, attention, reading duration, comprehension, belief, M1.E2 Pengage, or M0 Share probability.

definition: Reference M1.E3 binary outcome indicating whether the full item is opened/clicked after the preview impression.
what_it_is_not: Attention, reading completion, endorsement, belief, active-engagement intent, or sharing.

definition: Registered event that the headline preview was rendered/available in the M1.E3 reference task.
what_it_is_not: Proof of visual fixation, reading, encoding, recall, or full-content access.

definition: Normative probability assigned to a binary proposition before the current diagnostic evidence item when the task supplies a defensible probabilistic prior.
what_it_is_not: The descriptive CEM belief B, ground truth, or population prevalence unless a task explicitly defines it that way.

definition: Externally supplied diagnostic ratio P(evidence|proposition true) / P(evidence|proposition false) from a defensible task-specific measurement model.
what_it_is_not: Source trust, familiarity, amount of evidence, social agreement, salience, or subjective confidence.

definition: Normative binary proposition probability after a declared prior is updated with one or more defensible diagnostic likelihood ratios.
what_it_is_not: VAR.BELIEF.CLAIM B, knowledge, truth, ideology, or a calibrated population opinion.

definition: Normalized binary Shannon entropy derived from Pwm, equal to one at p=0.5 and zero at p=0 or p=1.
what_it_is_not: The decision-uncertainty registry, metacognitive confidence, model misspecification, or unknown unknowns.

definition: Traceable record of an evidence item, source, acquisition context, and measurement assumptions relevant to a world-model update.
what_it_is_not: Objective truth certification or the agent-relative source-reliability estimate T.
